title: Veridian Health - Integration Launchpad Sync
summary: Kickoff sync to align launchpad/pilot plan for Veridian Health's private deployment. Covered VPC peering windows, minimal bench targets (95th pct < 150ms for short prompts), data residency constraints, SOC2 evidence request, and runbook ownership. Agreed on two-week pilot with targeted endpoints and a fall-back plan to hosted during initial rollout.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-09 15:00 PST | Duration 48m | Recording: auto
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (CSM), Samir (SE); Evelyn, Marcus, Rita, Noah (Veridian)
---
00:00 Jordan: okay hi everybody thanks for making the time today um we wanted to run through the launchpad plan for the private deployment and make sure we align on the network windows and the pilot scope
00:18 Evelyn: yeah thanks Jordan, I appreciate you doing this. we've got a few folks from platform and security because we want to make sure we don't surprise our infra team
00:26 Marcus: hey all, Marcus here. quick heads up we've got a maintenance window on 11/18 that might affect peering but otherwise we're good to schedule
00:34 Jordan: perfect, we'll call that out. Priya and Samir are with me from Redwood, Samir will handle the technical bits — the runtime, quantization options, that sort of thing
00:45 Samir: hi everyone, and quick note — we'll try to keep the deep kernel/quant stuff high level unless you want a follow-up SE session
00:53 Rita: definitely want to cover compliance, so SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration patterns, and audit logs. we circled back with legal last night, they want specifics
01:05 Priya: great, we have a security packet and an on-prem checklist; i'll share links after the call. also we'll include a sample runbook template
01:15 Noah: on the pilot itself — what's the proposed success criteria? latency, cost, accuracy?
01:22 Jordan: those are all good. for the initial two-week pilot we're suggesting 95th percentile < 150ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and throughput of ~200 requests/min for the primary endpoint. cost targets we'll model after your expected QPS, samir can talk about batching and caching to hit unit-cost goals
01:42 Samir: yeah, automatic prefix caching and a modest batching window should help reduce tokens per inference. note that for our private deployments we can recommend either 16-bit quant or 8-bit quant profiles depending on your accuracy tolerance
01:55 Marcus: do you have benchmark numbers for 8-bit vs 16-bit on a T4-like instance? our fleet is mostly g4dn right now
02:05 Samir: rough numbers: 8-bit tends to shave ~30-40% memory and 10-20% latency on streaming, but you might see a slight regression on some instruction-heavy prompts. we'll run model-specific bench with your corpus and share a spreadsheet
02:21 Evelyn: that would be great — sample prompts will be uploaded to the shared drive after this meeting
02:28 Jordan: noted. network questions — Rita, what's your main concern around VPC peering?
02:34 Rita: we need egress control and proof that logs are captured centrally. also key management — can we bring our own KMS/HSM?
02:42 Samir: yes BYOK is supported for the private control plane; on the inference hosts we integrate with KMS for secret provisioning. logs are emitted to a customer-controlled syslog or S3 with configurable retention
02:54 Rita: ok, retention policy is important. we need 7 years of audit trail for certain flows — will that be an add-on?
03:02 Priya: retention beyond default is part of an add-on compliance package; i'll include estimated pricing in the follow-up packet
03:09 Noah: also curious about graceful degradation — if dedicated capacity is saturated during a spike what happens?
03:15 Jordan: we support smart routing and fallbacks: policy-based routing can fail over to a compatible hosted model or queue requests, depending on how you prefer to prioritize latency versus cost
03:26 Marcus: can we control that per route? we have different SLAs per product line
03:29 Samir: yes per-route policies — can do canary, failover, or wait-and-retry. we'll show the console demo in a follow-up but you can specify thresholds like p95 > X ms -> failover to hosted
03:41 Evelyn: timing — what's the earliest we can start the two-week pilot?
03:46 Jordan: assuming network approval and a quick account setup, we can start as early as 11/22, but given Marcus's maintenance window we'll aim for 11/27 unless you want us to start in a partial capacity
03:55 Marcus: 11/27 works better for us
03:58 Rita: legal will need SOC2 docs before we do any data in the pilot. also we need an MSA redline — procurement will be involved
04:07 Priya: i'll share the SOC2 summary and the customer-facing security packet today; Jordan will loop in legal templates. can we get a point of contact from procurement?
04:16 Rita: that's me, Rita. we'll try to turn the MSA redline in 5 business days
04:21 Jordan: awesome. responsibilities — i'm assuming Priya will drive runbook ownership and Samir will handle the bench setup
04:27 Priya: yes i'll draft the runbook and share a first pass by 11/15
04:31 Samir: i'll coordinate the performance bench and send the spreadsheet with results and config knobs within 72 hours of getting the prompt set
04:39 Noah: for the bench — can we also test failure scenarios? like KV cache eviction or node preemption?
04:46 Samir: good call — we'll include a failure test matrix: cache misses, preemption, and noisy-neighbor scenarios. we'll label each with expected recovery behavior
04:55 Jordan: let's talk about routing and pinning — you'll want to pin model versions during the pilot to avoid surprises from upstream updates
05:02 Evelyn: yes pinning is necessary for us because we validate outputs against clinical prompt sets. how do we roll forward a new model?
05:09 Samir: we support canary rollouts with traffic splitting and automatic rollback on regressions. we also integrate eval hooks so you can run your test suite during a rollout
05:19 Marcus: any footprint concerns for our on-prem nodes? memory and disk I/O?
05:23 Samir: typical inference cache will need about X GiB per model shard — we'll give you exact numbers per model variant. on-disk caches are optional but speed up cold starts
05:34 Rita: encryption-in-transit and at-rest — standard TLS + AES256?
05:38 Samir: yes TLS1.3, AES256 at rest; KMS for key rotation. we can support HSM-backed keys on request
05:46 Priya: quick note — we have a runbook template that includes escalation phone numbers and a pager rotation example. we can adapt to your on-call flow
05:54 Noah: service levels — do you publish uptime SLAs for private installs?
05:58 Jordan: for private with enterprise package we provide an SLA backed commitment for control plane and a best-effort target for inference nodes; Dedicated reserved capacity has stronger SLOs. we'll include the SLA doc in the packet
06:10 Evelyn: on the data side, what about retention and PII? some prompts will include PHI, we need to ensure no persistent storage beyond the audit bucket
06:20 Samir: for PHI workflows we recommend private deployment with explicit retention and an option to disable ephemeral logging. we'll mark the audit trail only and avoid storing raw prompt texts unless you opt in
06:33 Rita: that sounds good — need to confirm with our DPO but seems aligned
06:39 Jordan: i'll capture that as part of the security packet notes. next — scheduling: we propose these milestones: runbook first pass 11/15, bench start 11/27, pilot window 11/27-12/10, pilot review 12/13
06:57 Marcus: that timeline is reasonable, gives us time to finish the MSA and network approvals
07:04 Priya: ok will add to calendar invites; i'll include Samir's bench template and a shared sprint board
07:12 Evelyn: one more thing — who on your side will be our day-to-day contact once the pilot starts?
07:18 Priya: i'll be the CSM owner and Jordan is your AE; Samir will be primary SE for technical escalations
07:24 Rita: sounds good. procurement will need a billing contact for the trial — Jordan, can you share that?
07:29 Jordan: yes i'll include billing contacts in the follow-up email and the pricing spreadsheet
07:34 Noah: do you have examples of runbooks from other health customers we can look at?
07:39 Priya: we can share a sanitized runbook sample — i'll attach it. note that patient data fields are redacted
07:46 Samir: technical note — if you plan to use long-context prompts >4k tokens we'll want to test memory and KV reuse patterns. those numbers impact both latency and cost
07:57 Marcus: our use cases are short clinical summaries, mostly under 400 tokens, but we have a few batch jobs that need longer context
08:06 Samir: fine, we'll include a mix in the bench set. also recommend enabling continuous batching for batch jobs and stream mode for low-latency RPCs
08:18 Jordan: ok wrapping up — can we do a quick recap of action items?
08:23 Priya: i'll share security packet, sample runbook, and sanitized runbook example today; first runbook draft 11/15
08:30 Samir: i'll start the bench after we get the prompt set on 11/27, send spreadsheet within 72 hours of bench run
08:36 Jordan: i'll send pricing spreadsheet, billing contact, and legal templates; loop in procurement and set the pilot window 11/27-12/10
08:45 Rita: procurement will aim to return MSA redline by 11/16
08:51 Evelyn: we'll upload prompts and evaluation criteria by 11/14
08:55 Noah: and we'll try to get network approvals in time for 11/22 but the official start will be 11/27 per Marcus
09:02 Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a calendar invite and the packet. Priya, Samir — anything else?
09:09 Priya: nothing else, thanks all
09:11 Samir: all good, thanks
09:13 Jordan: meeting adjourned
